title: Towards Unsupervised Domain Bridging via Image Degradation in Semantic Segmentation (DiDA)
mechanism: Build continuous intermediate domains by degrading images to graded strengths, so the network learns domain-shared features, with a diffusion-encoder term that compensates semantic shift; plugs into self-training UDA.
adaptation: Source = 478 labelled cells; target = 1,152 unlabelled multi half-cut pool cells (E1-like, not E1). Degradations chosen for EL: blur, gain, noise, vignetting. Put on top of the existing Mean Teacher code.
min_experiment: Arm: MT + DiDA on the half-cut pool, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF and the existing MT-with-pool run. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU; test crack IoU must not drop more than 0.012. Kill: E1 relF1@2 gain under 0.02 over PF.
evidence: R: consistent gains when added to several UDA methods on standard synthetic-to-real benchmarks (GTA/SYNTHIA to Cityscapes); exact numbers not read.
prior_overlap: Partial. Mean Teacher with the external pool was n.d. at 100% labels, but it was not aimed at E1 with target-like half-cut cells. BRIEF lists UDA aimed at E1 as open; per-panel BN adaptation (failed) is a different mechanism.
